column1: 12-2 IS–LM as a Theory of Aggregate Demand We have been using the IS–LM model to explain national income in the short run when the price level is fixed. To see how the IS–LM model fits into the model of aggregate supply and aggregate demand introduced in Chapter 10, we now examine what happens in the IS–LM model if the price level is allowed to change. By examining the effects of changing the price level, we can finally deliver what was promised when we began our study of the IS–LM model: a theory to explain the position and slope of the aggregate demand curve.
